subject: Temporary headroom waiver and queueing carveout request — Skyward Labs
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@skyward-labs.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skyward-labs.com
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary headroom waiver + queueing carveout for Dedicated SKU

Hi Chloe / Ben,

We're ramping a customer-facing AI feature next week and expect a sizable, short-lived spike in inference traffic (roughly 2.5x baseline QPS for ~48–72 hours). Skyward is on the Dedicated SKU (reserved GPU pool: 8 x rtx-dedicated nodes) and we want to avoid throttling that would degrade UX.

Specific asks:
- Is Redwood able to provision a temporary headroom waiver that prevents normal queueing preemption for this 48–72 hour window?
- If not fully possible, can you carve out a priority queue slice or use tokenized priority so our traffic gets through at a predictable latency?
- Any playbook or temporary addendum we should sign (procurement is on cc).

I've attached a CSV with our expected traffic profile and peak windows. Happy to jump on a quick call — launch target is 2026-06-10 10:00 PDT.

Attachments: headroom-request.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform
Skyward Labs

Subject: Re: Request: temporary headroom waiver + queueing carveout for Dedicated SKU

Hi Elena — thanks for the data and heads-up.

Quick answers up front: uptime SLA remains the same; this discussion is about reserved capacity behavior (queueing and priority) and whether we can temporarily relax preemption or provide a prioritized carveout.

Two immediate asks so we can scope the right playbook:
1) Can you confirm the expected sustained QPS and concurrent sessions during the 2–3 hour peak windows you listed in the CSV?
2) Which model families will you be serving (config affects KV cache and batch sizing)?

Proposed next steps: 30-minute call today or tomorrow to agree on a technical mitigation (priority tokens / short-term headroom / fallback model routing) and produce a short addendum procurement can sign. Ben — can you pull the standard temporary-headroom addendum and a draft priority-token playbook?

I copied procurement so we can align contract language (this should be a timeboxed operational carveout, not a permanent SLA change).

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Sun, Jun 7, 2026 at 09:14 Elena Torres <elena.torres@skyward-labs.com> wrote: > We're ramping ...

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@skyward-labs.com>, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, procurement@skyward-labs.com
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary headroom waiver + queueing carveout for Dedicated SKU

Elena / Chloe — thanks for the context. We're able to offer an interim operational plan that has been used for short launch spikes before. High-level proposal:

- Temporary headroom: allow 2x baseline reserved throughput for a 72-hour window starting 2026-06-10 08:00 PDT.
- Queueing carveout: allocate a tokenized priority lane for Skyward; tokens consumed only during the headroom window to minimize impact on other tenants.
- Fairness guard: automatic fallback to normal preemption if sustained excess beyond the 72 hours is detected; this protects other Dedicated customers.
- Credits: if we surface an SLA impact (queueing variance) on our side, Redwood will apply a one-time 15% usage credit for excess over committed baseline during the window (billed monthly).

I've attached a draft addendum (dedicated-sku-addendum-draft.docx) with precise timing, token definitions, and monitoring hooks (traces + dashboard link). If procurement signs, we can schedule the change and pre-warm caches and routing rules.

Proposed implementation plan (high level):
1) Sign addendum + PO -> 2) Pre-warm model caches 24 hours before start -> 3) Switch priority tokens on at start window -> 4) Monitor and escalate if tail latency exceeds agreed thresholds -> 5) Switch off at window end and apply credits if applicable.

Elena: does the 15% credit and 72-hour window look workable, or do you need a different tradeoff?

Attachments: dedicated-sku-addendum-draft.docx (DOCX)

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
